result.title: Training-Free Inference Acceleration for Video Large Language Models: Methods, Trade-offs, and Evaluation
result.summary: Video Large Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in video understanding and reasoning, but processing long visual sequences incurs substantial computational, latency, and memory overhead. This survey examines training-free inference acceleration, focusing on reducing inference costs while preserving task-relevant spatiotemporal evidence. We organize existing methods by their intervention stages in the inference pipeline, covering input, visual encoding, projector, prefill, and decoding. Post-training quantization (PTQ) is discussed separately as a cross-stage extension with varying calibration requirements. We analyze how intervention position affects evidence preservation and computational savings, and why local efficiency improvements may not translate into end-to-end acceleration. We complement this analysis with quantitative evidence from prior studies and our own experiments under a shared evaluation setting to assess accuracy-latency trade-offs.

AI.brief_summary: 该综述梳理视频大语言模型的免训练推理加速方法，按推理流程中的干预阶段（输入、视觉编码、projector、prefill、解码）组织，并单列 PTQ 作为跨阶段扩展；结合既有研究与统一设置下的自测实验，分析精度与延迟的权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对「干预位置如何影响任务相关时空证据保留」以及局部效率提升未必转化为端到端加速的分析，可能为 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的证据筛选与计算成本核算提供参照框架，可核查其评测口径能否迁移到 latent 推理场景。
